title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 418
paragraphs: So when the Ichthyophagoi had come to this people, they presented their gifts to the king who ruled over them and said: “The king of the Persians Cambyses, wishing to become your friend and guest-friend, sent us with orders to come and speak with you, and he gives you these gifts, which are the things he himself most delights to use.” The Ethiopian, however, perceiving that they had come as spies, spoke to them as follows: “Neither did the king of the Persians send you bearing gifts because he thought it a matter of great importance to become my guest-friend, nor do you speak the truth — for you have come as spies of my kingdom — nor again is he a righteous man; for if he were righteous, he would not have coveted a land other than his own, nor would he be leading men into slavery at whose hands he has suffered no wrong. Now then, give him this bow and say these words: The king of the Ethiopians gives this advice to the king of the Persians, that when the Persians can draw bows of this size as easily as I draw this one, then he may march against the Long-lived Ethiopians, provided he be superior in numbers; but until then, let him feel gratitude to the gods that they do not put it into the minds of the sons of the Ethiopians to acquire another land in addition to their own.”
